title: Control state must be consistent across sibling endpoints
context: GET /v1/models ignored Llm.Enabled while POST /v1/chat/completions honored it.
takeaway: When adding a policy toggle, check EVERY endpoint that should reflect it, not just the obvious one. Inconsistent enforcement is an audit finding.

title: Don't keep a trigger that can never succeed
context: Dashboard Mutate button dispatched CI that had no Claude login; every run failed exit 1.
takeaway: A green-looking control that always fails manufactures false evidence of work. Move execution to where the credential lives (local queue-and-drain) or disable it honestly. Evidence over assertion.

title: A passing test for a reported bug means the bug is elsewhere
context: Ticket #7: LuhnValid had no upper bound. Wrote a 22-digit regression test first; it passed before any fix because the card-candidate regex already clamps to {13,19} and the only other caller (SA-ID) is always 13 digits.
takeaway: When a test written to expose a bug passes immediately, do not declare victory — find out why. The real guard may be upstream. Fix the helper anyway as defense-in-depth, but describe the reachability honestly in the PR.

title: Frontend call site vs backend endpoint — check both ends
context: Issue #10: api.getGitRepos() was defined in the API object but never called in ScansRepos; and the backend had no /api/scans/git-repositories endpoint at all. The tab was empty for two independent reasons.
takeaway: When a UI feature is empty, diagnose both ends: (1) is the API function called in the component, (2) does the backend route exist. Either can be the culprit.

title: Shared WebApplicationFactory accumulates in-memory state across tests
context: Issue #30: the read-only test and POST test shared one factory. The POST test added a repo to the in-memory policy, causing the empty-list assertion to see count=1.
takeaway: Split tests that write shared state (policy store, audit log) from read-only tests: read tests share a ClassFixture, write tests get a fresh factory per test (new WebApplicationFactory<Program>())

title: PolicyStore disk persistence makes all test factories share state — use isolated temp policy files
context: Issue #33: GitRepoLinkTests and GitRepoReadTests factories all defaulted to the same policy.json on disk. Parallel xUnit tests caused concurrent writes and state leakage. The read test saw repos left by write tests from the same run.
takeaway: Any WebApplicationFactory that POSTs to the policy endpoint must be given a unique PolicyPath (Path.GetTempFileName()). Never let write tests share the disk-level policy.json with read tests. Create IsolatedPolicyFactory for shared read fixtures.

title: WSL git push needs token-in-URL workaround
context: git push via https failed in WSL because the credential helper couldn't read from the Windows keyring. gh.exe auth was fine but git couldn't use it.
takeaway: In WSL, if git push fails with 'could not read Username', extract the token via gh auth token and temporarily set the remote URL to https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/... — then restore the clean URL after push.
